explanations: The wire format's recorded_at is Unix time in seconds, and encodeReading writes it that way (getTime() / 1000). But decodeTimestamp passes the number straight to new Date(), which expects milliseconds, so a gateway timestamp like 1795089510 decodes to a moment in January 1970. Ingest then rejects every gateway reading as more than 24 hours old, and encode-then-decode doesn't round-trip. Old firmware sends ISO strings, which take the other branch, so those trucks were unaffected. Multiplying the numeric value by 1000 before building the Date makes decoding match the documented unit and the encoder.
